classification.difficultyReason: Justifies unchanged triangle area by recognising that movement parallel to the fixed base preserves perpendicular height.

inlines.text: , for this triangle moves parallel to the base
Will the area of the triangle change? Justify your answer.
(Hint: Think about the lengths of the base and the height).

spec.description: Triangle ABC with horizontal base AB. A horizontal movement line through C has arrowheads at both ends and seven red position dots. Additional arrows point outward beside the label C, and a right-pointing arrow lies on AB.
spec.mathematics: The vertex moves along a line parallel to the fixed base, preserving perpendicular height and triangle area.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, labels, arrows and position markers are permanent question givens; the justification appears only in answer fields.

answer.short: No. The base and height do not change.
answer.worked: The base $AB$ is fixed. Moving $C$ parallel to $AB$ keeps the perpendicular height the same, so $A=\frac{bh}{2}$ is unchanged.
